sources.entry: Gifski - Convert videos to high-quality GIFs.

summary.one_liner: A macOS app that converts videos into high-quality animated GIFs using the gifski encoder, with optional gifsicle-based lower-quality output.
summary.what_it_does: Gifski is a Mac app wrapping the gifski encoder, which uses pngquant's cross-frame palettes and temporal dithering to produce GIFs with thousands of colors per frame and up to 50 FPS. A Quality slider can produce smaller, lower-quality GIFs via gifsicle. It accepts any video format macOS supports, such as MP4 or MOV with H264, HEVC, or ProRes, but not QuickTime Animation or WebM. Settings include dimensions, speed, frame rate, quality, cropping, and looping. It also offers a bounce (yo-yo) playback option that doubles the frame count, plus a share extension, a Services menu item, and a Finder Quick Action shortcut.
use_cases: Convert a screen recording or video clip to a GIF on a Mac
Make high-frame-rate animated GIFs for showing design work
Shrink GIF file size by lowering quality, dimensions, or FPS
Convert a PNG sequence to GIF via FFmpeg and Gifski
Batch-convert videos from Finder or the Shortcuts app
how_to_run: curl -sSf | sh (install Rust, per README; URL is incomplete in the source)
Open the project in Xcode and build the app
notable: Cross-frame palettes and temporal dithering for high-quality GIFs with thousands of colors per frame
Up to 50 FPS output, with an explanation that higher rates are throttled by browsers
Share extension, Services menu item, and Finder Quick Action shortcut
Bounce (yo-yo) playback mode that doubles the frame count
Non-App Store version available for users who cannot access the App Store
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later for the current version; older versions support earlier macOS releases
The Quick Action shortcut requires the TestFlight version of Gifski
Does not support WebM, QuickTime Animation, or Windows/Linux; a cross-platform command-line tool is mentioned but not named
GIF files can be very large; works best with short clips
